newsitem.title: INDIA: S.Africa's Mbeki to visit India to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki to visit India to boost ties.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will arrive in the Indian capital this week to strengthen trade and investment cooperation, the South African embassy said on Sunday.
Mbeki will meet Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, President Shankar Dayal Sharma and hold talks with External Affairs Minister Inder Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram.

The visit, for five days from December 3, coincides with the second meeting of the South Africa-India Joint Commission, which will focus on political relations, defence, trade and technology, an embassy statement said.

Mbeki, who will be accompanied by Trade Minister Alec Erwin and Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna, is likely to sign agreements on avoidance of double taxation, promotion and protection of investment and a memorandum of understanding on defence cooperation.
He is also scheduled to go to Bombay and Bangalore.
In Bombay, the country's financial capital, he will meet the country's top industrialists, the statement said.
Trade between India and South Africa has increased by 560 percent since 1993, the statement said.
South Africa and India are among several states advocating greater cooperation among Indian Ocean rim countries, particularly in the fields of tourism, technology, air transport, banking and finance.
